argument: Refute, and a correction to round 1's scope: the chapter teaches the Defend maneuver two incompatible ways, and the deviant statement sits in the lookup table players actually use. The Basic Maneuvers table grants a Boon on the defense roll until the character's next turn; both worked-example uses of the maneuver apply that Boon; and the chapter's quick-reference maneuver table repeats the Boon wording, so four surfaces agree. Only the Defend row of the Defense Roll Modifiers summary converts the same maneuver into a flat plus two. Under the locked dice law those are not the same rule, since a Boon is a four-die keep-highest-three roll rather than a modifier, so a reader looking up defense math in the summary gets a procedure the maneuver table and the play example contradict. This is an internal contradiction within one chapter, not an open conversion question: the book has already settled the Boon form and the summary cell is the outlier to conform. Round 1 saw it and let it pass; none of the seven shipped findings files it, and the t-02 set covers only the undefined escape action, the dying procedure and the wound table. The companion row in that same summary, Surprised at minus two, is a cross-chapter matter against chapter 19 and belongs to a t-03 lens. Repair is one cell, or the maneuver plus its example instead if a flat bonus is the real intent; either way the chapter cannot ship teaching both.

evidence.claim: The Basic Maneuvers table defines Defend as granting a Boon on the user's defense roll until their next turn.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Boon on your Defense roll until your next turn.

evidence.claim: The defense modifiers summary prices the same maneuver as a flat plus two lasting one round, the only surface in the book that does so.
Both worked-example uses of the maneuver resolve it as a Boon on defense rather than a flat bonus, so the chapter's own teaching text sides with the maneuver table.

evidence.claim: The at-table maneuver reference repeats the Boon wording verbatim, so the chapter is split internally and the tiebreak material agrees with the Boon, not the plus two.
